items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: I knew him personally. He was my friend.

ctx.x: But did you know Louis Armstrong? Did you ever know him?

I knew him personally. He was my friend. Well when he was at the play down here, I was listening to him and he says, I'd like to dedicate this next number to my little fat friend, Johnny Gidroyd. I was a little star at that time, you know, and he called me his fat. And then I met him in New York, and we were palsy-weldy, and I loved to hear him play. And when he was on the coast, my brother used to go out to the cotton club and they were friends. And he was one of the finest men I ever met, I mean as far as I know.
But did you know him in New York you say?

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: I mean I'm like Louis Armstrong and I'm a contemporary. I helped him when he had patches in his pants.

ctx.x: I mean I'm like Louis Armstrong and I'm a contemporary. I helped him when he had patches in his pants. I helped many a colored man. I remember, I know he published Don't Mean a Thing If You Ain't Got That Swing, because I played the first three of them, Clarence Williams. And when I went to New York to play at Healy's Balkanades, and he called me up and he said, Johnny I've got some new tunes and they just fit you, and if you don't mind I'll come to rehearsal and tell you how I think they should be played. Not…
